string.text: A human is not a truck and cannot carry a ton on their back. The more they carry, the greater the fatigue and the faster they lose strength. Eventually, if there are too many items, it will be difficult to even move.

If you stay in an area with a high radiation background or carry a radioactive artifact with you, signs of radiation exposure appear. As a result, your health begins to decrease. To remove the effects of radiation exposure, you need to use anti-rad medication or vodka.

If you carry many heavy items, fatigue gradually begins to build up. When fatigue becomes severe, it will be impossible to run or even walk for some time. Strength can be partially restored by resting briefly while standing still. Only sleep will fully restore strength.

When the body is hit (by bullets, animal claws, and so on), bleeding begins. Bleeding is a constant loss of health. The more severe the bleeding (green icon — light bleeding, red — heavy bleeding), the more health is lost per unit of time. Only minor bleeding stops on its own; most bleeding can be stopped using bandages.

A heavy blow, a bite or a bullet to an arm, a leg or the head can leave an injury. Damage adds up: several weak bites in a row will cripple too, but a limb recovers if it takes no new hits for a while. Bones are broken by bullets, explosions and the heaviest blows - like a boar's charge; bites cripple but do not break. An injured arm: the weapon sways more, reloading and switching weapons are slower. An injured leg: walking and running are slower, and a broken leg cannot sprint at all. A blow to the head stuns for a while. A light injury heals by itself in half an hour once the limb is patched up to at least three quarters. A plain medkit clears it at once. A fracture is set with a splint, a survival kit or an army medkit. In a splint you can run, if slower, and the bone knits in a day - twice as fast while asleep. A scientific medkit sets two fractures at once. Untreated, the bone sets crookedly by itself in two days, and then it is like a splint. Sidorovich and Barman sell splints.

Artifacts and bandages patch you up in a hurry: that health is shown in green. It holds - it counts for total health and keeps you alive, and wounds take it first. But it does not heal the limb: legs with green health still move like wounded ones, and a light injury will not heal by itself until the limb is properly treated. Temporary health slowly turns permanent by itself, faster with strong artifacts. A medkit fixes it at once: a plain one half, an army one three quarters, a scientific one all of it. Sleep fixes all of it. The health bar on the watch and in the backpack shows the greatest danger: if the head or the torso is weaker than the body on average, the bar shows them. Wounds to the head and torso are what kill.

Pain builds up from wounds, blows and fractures and slowly fades by itself. Strong pain steals your breath: stamina recovers slower and your hands shake. At its limit it knocks you out - and you will not come round soon. The pain level is shown in the backpack under the figure. Morphine relieves pain strongly, vodka a little. Fractures hurt until they are treated.

After a heavy wound, or when health is nearly gone, the body releases adrenaline. For half a minute pain does not grow and you cannot pass out, you get a burst of stamina, and you can run on a broken leg, limping. Your hands shake, though. Once the fight is over, after about a minute without shots or wounds, the crash comes: stamina drains, the hands tremble, part of the held-back pain returns. The next rush comes no sooner than five minutes later. The outer frame of the watch shows the adrenaline left.
